chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban from Ibn Hakim from Abu Ibrahim or his father (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding the divorced woman, her husband divorces her and she says, 'I am pregnant,' so she remains for a year. He said: If she brings him after more than a year, she will not be believed, even if it is one hour in her claim.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a divorced woman claims pregnancy after more than a year?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the maximum gestation period (uddat al-waladah) as one year for a divorced woman, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence for determining paternity and inheritance. It clarifies that a claim of delayed birth beyond this limit is rejected even by a single hour, emphasizing the precision required in legal testimony regarding lineage. This ruling aligns with the majority view of the Imams and serves as a foundational text for discussions on the variability of pregnancy duration in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban, from Ibn Hakeem, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7th Imam<sup>asws</sup>), or from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup>

having said with regards to the divorced woman, her husband divorces her so she is saying, ‘I am pregnant’. So she remains for a year’, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she comes with him after more than a year, she would not be ratified, even if it is one hour in her claim’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Hakim who has said the following: “About the case of a woman who is divorced and she claims to be pregnant; so she waits for one year, abu Ibrahim or his father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If she comes up with such claim after a year it is not accepted even if it is one hour more.’”
